title: Chart-adjunction pullbacks realize normalized ringed tensors
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$, $k:Z\to X$ morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the chart direct images $D_l$, specified left adjoints $P_l\dashv D_l$, units $\eta^l$, and chart projections $\pi^l$ of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], for $l=f,k,fk$. Write $Q_l$ for ringed module direct image in the enlarged etale model [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], transported to the small sites, and let $\alpha_l:D_l\simeq Q_l$ be the projection-preserving comparisons of [lem-trf-space-chart-limit-enlarged-sections]. Let $L_l=\mathcal O_{\mathrm{source}(l)}\otimes_{l^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathrm{target}(l)}}l^{-1}(-)$ be transported ringed tensor pullback [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with its usual adjunction unit $\eta^{\mathrm{ten},l}$. There is a unique natural isomorphism $\tau_l:P_l\simeq L_l$ satisfying $Q_l(\tau_{l,M})\alpha_{l,P_lM}\eta^l_M=\eta^{\mathrm{ten},l}_M$. For an etale scheme $V$ over the target, a chart $q=(T,a)\in\mathcal A(l,V)$, $m\in M(V)$ and $b\in\mathcal O(T)$, $\tau_l$ sends the unit-defined chart tensor $b\,\pi^l_q(\eta^l_M(m))$ to $b\otimes[m]_{q}$, where $[m]_q$ is the inverse-image section induced by the chart triangle $a:T\to V$. These formulas commute with chart restrictions and module maps. Under these three isomorphisms the canonical tensor-composition isomorphism $L_kL_f\simeq L_{fk}$ induces a natural isomorphism $P_kP_f\simeq P_{fk}$ whose local tensor formula is $a\otimes(b\otimes m)\mapsto a\,k^\sharp(b)\otimes m$ and whose inverse is $e\otimes m\mapsto e\otimes(1\otimes m)$. Here tensors mean local representatives of the sheafified tensor constructions; the assertion imposes no global pure-tensor representation on arbitrary sections. If $l:Z'\to Z$ is etale, these identifications realize its inverse-image structure ring as the restricted structure ring, with identical regular functions, ring operations and restrictions on every scheme object. The composite of $\tau_l$ with $\mathcal O_{Z'}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Z'}}(-|_{Z'})\simeq(-|_{Z'})$ sends $a\otimes m$ to $am$, has inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, and carries the specified chart-unit tensor to multiplication by $a$ of the restricted section. These maps satisfy the balancing identity $1\otimes am=a\otimes m$ locally before sheafification.

proof.text: Work first in the enlarged ringed sites and then conjugate functors and Hom bijections by their specified module equivalences. The enlarged-model theorem supplies the geometric inverse images, structural ring maps and smallness relative to module sheaves. Apply the ringed-topos module adjunction with $R=\widetilde{\mathcal O}_{\mathrm{target}(l)}$ and $S=\widetilde{\mathcal O}_{\mathrm{source}(l)}$ for each $l=f,k,fk$. It gives $L_l\dashv Q_l$. The chart-limit theorem gives the natural $\alpha_l:D_l\simeq Q_l$ preserving the actual restrictions to every chart, including the coefficient action through $a^\sharp$. Thus this adjunction concerns the specified direct images, rather than unrelated isomorphic objects.

Fix the unit of this tensor adjunction explicitly. For $I_l=l^{-1}$ on algebraic modules and a module map $h:S\otimes_{I_lR}I_lM\to H$, the scalar-extension transpose is $x\mapsto h(1\otimes x)$: the sectionwise extension/restriction bijection gives this formula, and module sheafification gives its unique sheaf version. The geometric-module transpose then applies the underlying geometric Hom bijection, by its stated normalization. At $h=1_{L_lM}$ the result is therefore the geometric inverse-image unit followed by scalar insertion $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. In particular its projection along $q=(T,a)$ sends $m\in M(V)$ to $1\otimes[m]_q$: the geometric unit at $V$ inserts $m$, and restriction along $T\to X\times_YV$ gives the inverse-image section denoted $[m]_q$. This describes $\eta^{\mathrm{ten},l}$, without an assumption that arbitrary tensor-sheaf sections are pure tensors.

source.place: Tags 03D3 (lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules), 03D7 and 03CZ (lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict); scalar formula Algebra Tag 05DQ

proof.text: Apply the unit-compatible uniqueness theorem with $(L_1,R_1)=(P_l,D_l)$, $(L_2,R_2)=(L_l,Q_l)$ and $\delta=\alpha_l^{-1}$. It produces a unique natural isomorphism $\tau_l:P_l\simeq L_l$ with $D_l(\tau_{l,M})\eta^l_M=\alpha_{l,L_lM}^{-1}\eta^{\mathrm{ten},l}_M$. Naturality of $\alpha_l$ at $\tau_{l,M}$ rewrites this precisely as $Q_l(\tau_{l,M})\alpha_{l,P_lM}\eta^l_M=\eta^{\mathrm{ten},l}_M$. Conversely the displayed equation implies the uniqueness theorem's equation by multiplying by $\alpha_{l,L_lM}^{-1}$, so it determines $\tau_l$ uniquely.

Project the equation of Step 3 to $q$. By the projection-preserving property of $\alpha_l$ and Step 2, it reads $\tau_{l,M,T}(\pi^l_q(\eta^l_M(m)))=1\otimes[m]_q$. Since $\tau_{l,M,T}$ is $\mathcal O(T)$-linear, multiplying by $b$ gives exactly $b\otimes[m]_q$. If $r:T\prime\to T$ is a chart restriction, both sides restrict to $r^\sharp(b)\otimes[m]_{q\prime}$; if $M\to N$ is a module map, both sides become $b\otimes[\varphi_V(m)]_q$. These follow respectively from the stated naturality of the chart cones and from naturality of the unit and $\tau_l$. They prove all the requested chart and coefficient naturality.

source.place: Tag 03D7 and spaces-properties.tex Tag 03G8; elementary projection of the unit equation

proof.text: For composition, use the enlarged-model composition of ringed topoi: after the canonical inverse-image comparison the structural map is $k^\sharp\circ k^{-1}(f^\sharp)$. The algebraic inverse-image tensor theorem identifies $k^{-1}(\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}f^{-1}M)$ with $k^{-1}\mathcal O_X\otimes_{k^{-1}f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}k^{-1}f^{-1}M$, preserving pure tensors. The sheaf inverse-image composition comparison sends nested inverse-image representatives to their composite representative, as stated by the composition-generators theorem. Consequently, writing $R=k^{-1}f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$, $B=k^{-1}\mathcal O_X$, $C=\mathcal O_Z$ and $N=k^{-1}f^{-1}M$, the two tensor constructions become $C\otimes_B(B\otimes_RN)$ and $C\otimes_RN$, using the specified ring maps. These are identifications of sheafified tensors; none asserts that evaluation on a site object preserves tensor products.

On these tensor presentations put $\mu(a\otimes(b\otimes n))=a\,k^\sharp(b)\otimes n$ and $
u(e\otimes n)=e\otimes(1\otimes n)$. The outer balancing relation moves $b\in B$ into $C$; the inner relation $(br)\otimes n=b\otimes rn$ maps to the $R$-balancing relation in $C\otimes_RN$, since the composite ring map is the one in Step 5. The same $R$ relation makes $
u$ well defined. Both formulas are additive in each variable and commute with restrictions. First extend the inner balanced pairing across its sheafification, then the outer pairing across its sheafification; the universal property gives the required sheaf maps. For the inverse use the single balanced pairing and its sheafification. Now $\mu
u(e\otimes n)=e\otimes n$, while $
u\mu(a\otimes(b\otimes n))=a\,k^\sharp(b)\otimes(1\otimes n)=a\otimes(b\otimes n)$ by outer balancing. The equalities on tensor generators extend by additivity and the sheafification universal property. Thus $\mu$ is the normalized natural tensor-composition isomorphism and $
u$ its inverse.

proof.text: The induced comparison on the specified left adjoints is the composite $P_kP_fM\xrightarrow{\tau_{k,P_fM}}L_kP_fM\xrightarrow{L_k(\tau_{f,M})}L_kL_fM\xrightarrow{\mu_M}L_{fk}M\xrightarrow{\tau_{fk,M}^{-1}}P_{fk}M$. It is a natural isomorphism since every factor is. Steps 4 and 6 give its local formulas, including the inverse $e\otimes m\mapsto e\otimes(1\otimes m)$. To check the canonical normalization, the two successive tensor units insert $1\otimes(1\otimes m)$ and $\mu$ carries this to $1\otimes m$. With the composite-adjunction unit formula this is the unit of the composite ringed morphism; uniqueness therefore identifies $\mu$ with the adjunction-compatible compositor. This also verifies the normalization when either morphism is the identity.

source.place: Tag 03D8, with the unit formula for composition and Tag 0B65

proof.text: Finally let $u:Z\prime\to Z$ be etale. The enlarged-model theorem identifies its site with $\mathcal C_Z/Z\prime$, its geometric inverse image with restriction, and its structural ring map with the identity on the restricted structure sheaf. On each scheme object $T\to Z\prime$ both structure rings are $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ with identical operations and restrictions. Hence the tensor construction is $\mathcal O_{Z\prime}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Z\prime}}(M|_{Z\prime})$. Multiplication $a\otimes m\mapsto am$ is balanced and inverse to $m\mapsto1\otimes m$: one composite is $m\mapsto m$, and the other is $a\otimes m\mapsto1\otimes am=a\otimes m$ by balancing. These equalities hold already in each tensor presheaf and hence in its sheafification. Step 4 carries the specified chart-unit tensor to $a\otimes m$, so its composite with multiplication is $am$, as required.
